newsitem.title: USA: Tour sees more freeze damage in SW Kansas wheat.
newsitem.headline: Tour sees more freeze damage in SW Kansas wheat.

text.p: Up to 50 percent of the hard red winter wheat crop in the extreme southwest corner of Kansas was damaged by a mid-April freeze, Wheat Quality Council crop scouts said after touring four fields there.
"The further south we came, the lack of snow cover and the advanced maturity of the crop made the freeze more severe," said Merle Koehn, operations manager for Grain Growers Coop in Montezuma, Kan.

After touring two fields in Morton County, scouts said freeze damage estimates varied from superficial in the northern part of the county to roughly 50 percent loss of production potential in the central part.
Tiller counts had indicated a yield count of up to 40 bushels per acre in Morton County but heavy freeze damage to those tillers cut crop forecasts nearly in half, scouts said.

In west-central Kansas, damage was not as severe. Tour participants noted fields there had been protected by snow cover when freezing temperatures on April 12-13 struck and the crop was not as mature as that seen further south.
Yield potential in Hamilton and Stanton counties in west-central Kansas was variable, ranging from roughly 25 to 40 bushels per acre, crop scouts said.
Fields toured in Stanton County appeared to have roughly 15 to 20 percent freeze damage.
